subject: Confirm downtime window and SLA credit eligibility
messages:
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Timothy Li <timothy.li@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected availability drop - 2026-06-25 morning

Hi Soojin,

We saw a significant increase in 503s and a spike in tail latency across several inference routes this morning between ~02:45 and ~03:30 UTC (our monitoring shows higher error rates and request timeouts during that window). This affected our customer-facing recommendation API and caused degraded UX for a subset of users.

Can you confirm whether this maps to an incident on Redwood's side and advise if this is eligible for SLA credit under our contract? We need the confirmed downtime window and an initial estimate for impact so we can start internal reporting.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Jensen
SRE Lead, Acme CloudOps

[Attachment: acme-monitoring-sample-20260625.png]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected availability drop - 2026-06-25 morning

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the sample graphs.

I'm escalating this to our on-call infra team to validate whether there was an outage affecting your tenant and to gather precise timing. Can you share the request IDs or a short span of example timestamps (in UTC) for a couple of failed requests? That will speed up correlation.

I'll loop back with an initial confirmation and whether this meets the SLA threshold (we'll be checking the 5-minute rolling availability metric per contract).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected availability drop - 2026-06-25 morning

On Thu, Jun 25, 2026 at 09:28 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'm escalating this to our on-call infra team to validate whether there was an outage affecting your tenant and to gather precise timing.

Hi Sarah — I pulled the routing logs for ACME from 02:30-04:00 UTC and forwarded them to Dev. Preliminary look shows elevated queue times on a subset of shards and a brief failure of a sidecar that pushes health metrics to the autoscaler (we saw a short flurry of 502s and then a larger number of 503s while autoscaler rebalanced).

I asked Dev to produce the exact downtime window and the raw request counts. If confirmed, we'll calculate the outage duration per the SLA (per-route 5-minute rolling availability) and provide a credit estimate.

-Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 02:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident confirmation: 2026-06-25 02:44-03:18 UTC (ACME tenant)

Team —

Root confirmation: between 02:44:12 UTC and 03:18:03 UTC we observed request error rates above the SLA threshold for tenant acme-corp on routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Cause: transient sidecar health-reporting failure combined with a delayed autoscaler reconciliation for affected GPU pools.

What I've attached:
- redwood-uptime-20260625.csv (per-route availability sampled per minute)
- incident-log-20260625.txt (system events, kube events, autoscaler activity)

Notes: we retried to mitigate; traffic was progressively relocated to standby nodes; service restored to normal after 03:18 UTC. We are preparing a more detailed postmortem with timeline and remediation items.

Dev
Dev Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-uptime-20260625.csv, incident-log-20260625.txt]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>, Timothy Li <timothy.li@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: SLA credit eligibility and next steps

Hi Sarah / Tim —

Thanks for your patience. Per Dev's confirmation, the affected window is 02:44:12–03:18:03 UTC on 2026-06-25. Based on our SLA (per-route 5-minute rolling availability), this event results in an availability drop that crosses the credit threshold for two routes.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood will run the formal credit calculation against the attached per-minute availability CSV and provide a dollar credit and invoice guidance by EOD Monday.
2) We will share a full postmortem with timeline, root cause, and remediation actions when the draft is ready (target: 2026-06-29).
3) If you need interim evidence for your incident report, Dev's incident-log attachment should suffice for now.

Marcus — can you confirm approval for issuing the credit once the calculation is complete?

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA credit eligibility and next steps

Confirmed. Approve issuing credit to Acme per the SLA once the calculation is done. Please proceed and copy finance for the final invoice adjustment.

Also linking the postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/ACME-20260625 — it's in shared view for Acme reviewers.

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: approval-note.txt]
